conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Rachel—one of the perinatal mental-health clinicians here. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, because emotional ups and downs are incredibly common and we want to be sure you’re getting whatever support you might need.

Everything you share stays confidential between you and the care team; the goal is to create a safe, judgment-free space. We’ll go through ten gentle questions about the past seven days—no right or wrong answers, just whatever feels true for you. It usually takes just a few minutes, and we can pause or rephrase anything if you need.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first question:

Over the last seven days, have you still been able to look forward with enjoyment to things, or has that felt harder to do?

Honestly, it’s felt a lot harder. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just watching a show I like—but lately it feels like I’m just going through the motions. I still try, but it’s like the joy isn’t really there.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I can laugh sometimes—mostly when my partner or my mom does something silly to cheer me up—but I have to really force it. It feels kind of hollow, like I’m pretending to find things funny even when I don’t feel it inside.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
Not really… I mean, I tell myself I should be excited about little outings or even just a quiet shower, but mostly I feel flat, like nothing seems worth looking forward to anymore.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that a lot. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m not doing something right—like I’m already failing him. Even little stuff, like spilling a bottle or being late to an appointment, I’ll replay in my head and tell myself I should be better at this.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s not breathing right, or I’ll lie awake picturing him rolling off the changing table even when he’s strapped in. I know it’s unlikely, but I can’t stop the “what-ifs” from looping.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes—those waves come out of nowhere. My chest gets tight, my hands shake, and suddenly I’m convinced something awful is about to happen to the baby, even when everything looks fine. It feels like I’m stuck in that moment until I pace around or turn on a light and remind myself we’re both okay.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, honestly. I’ll look at the pile of laundry or hear him start to cry and feel like I’m drowning—like I can’t catch my breath. I usually manage to get through it, but it’s this constant weight that never quite lifts.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I’ll finally get him down, but then my mind just keeps spinning with all the ways I might mess up tomorrow, or I replay every little thing I did wrong that day. Some nights I watch the clock roll past two, three, four a.m. before I drift off for an hour or two.
I have felt sad or miserable

That about sums it up. I feel weepy most of the day, like there’s this gray cloud hanging over everything. Even when I’m holding the baby—something I thought would feel magical—I just feel heavy and tearful.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s been happening a few times a week. Sometimes it’s because I’m overwhelmed, sometimes I just look at him and start crying because I feel like I’m already letting him down. The tears come and I can’t seem to shut them off.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’m exhausted and down, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like myself again so I can be the mom he deserves.

You've shared how the past week has felt heavy and joyless-laughing takes effort, outings feel pointless, and a constant gray cloud of <sym>sadness</sym> and <sym>self-blame</sym> hangs over each day. Even precious moments with your baby are tinged with <sym>tearfulness</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, and a sense that you're somehow failing him. The nights are the hardest, with racing thoughts keeping you awake until dawn, and waves of panic arriving uninvited. It's clear you're working incredibly hard to care for your little one while feeling overwhelmed and depleted, and that burden is understandably taking its toll.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 24, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient reports only occasional laughter with effort and describes it as hollow, matching "Definitely not so much now"</sym>, <sym>Patient expresses anhedonia with phrases like "nothing seems worth looking forward to" and persistent emotional flatness, aligning with "Hardly at all"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes frequent, pervasive self-blame across multiple daily situations, consistent with "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports daily, intrusive, uncontrollable anxious thoughts about the baby, matching the highest frequency option "Yes, very often"</sym>, <sym>Response describes frequent, intense panic attacks with physical symptoms and catastrophic thoughts, aligning with "Yes, quite a lot".</sym>, <sym>Patient reports feeling overwhelmed "most days" and uses vivid imagery of drowning, indicating significant difficulty coping, aligning with "sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual."</sym>, <sym>Patient describes frequent, prolonged insomnia due to persistent anxious thoughts, aligning with 'most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>Response explicitly reports feeling miserable "most of the day" with pervasive tearfulness and emotional heaviness, directly aligning with "Yes, most of the time."</sym>, <sym>Patient reports crying multiple times per week, aligning with "Yes, quite often"</sym>)
**Reasoning:** An EPDS total of 24 places you well above the ≥14 threshold indicating probable major <med>postpartum depression</med>. Your descriptions align with <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>: diminished interest/pleasure (<sym>anhedonia</sym>), depressed mood most of the day, recurrent thoughts of worthlessness/guilt, fatigue, insomnia, and marked <sym>anxiety</sym>. The combination of high-frequency anxious items (Q4, Q5) and core mood items (Q2, Q3, Q7, Q8) underscores a clinically significant mixed depression-anxiety presentation that warrants prompt evaluation and treatment. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with your <med>obstetrician</med> or <med>primary care provider</med> within the next few days for full diagnostic assessment
2. Request referral to a <med>perinatal mental-health specialist</med> for evidence-based therapy (CBT or interpersonal therapy) and discussion of medication options compatible with breastfeeding if desired
3. Begin gentle daily structure: short outdoor walks, balanced meals, and enlist your partner or family to cover one uninterrupted 4-hour sleep stretch
4. Keep crisis support numbers handy: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (24 h) and Postpartum Support International at 1-800-944-4773 (text 800-944-4773, English/en español)
5. Return for repeat EPDS screening in 2-3 weeks or sooner if mood worsens, self-harm thoughts arise, or you feel unable to care for yourself or your baby
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum parent (partner & maternal support noted)  
Date: Today  

I. Endorsed Symptoms/Concerns  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia (Q2, Q8, Q9)  
- Forced/“hollow” affect and loss of spontaneous laughter (Q1)  
- Pathologic guilt & self-blame regarding infant care (Q3)  
- Marked generalized & perinatal-specific anxiety with daily panic spells (Q4, Q5)  
- Sleep-onset insomnia secondary to rumination (Q7)  
- Sense of being overwhelmed / “drowning” (Q6)  

II. Pattern Summary  
Symptom cluster consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; no evidence of psychosis or mania.  

III. Safety  
Denies self-harm or suicidal ideation (Q10). No current safety concern reported.  

IV. Screening Significance  
EPDS equivalent score estimate ≈ 11–12 (anxiety items) + 7–8 (depression items) → total in high-risk range. Meets threshold for expedited referral for full diagnostic evaluation and evidence-based intervention (CBT/interpersonal therapy ± medication).  

V. Plan / Next Steps  
- Provide psychoeducation; review of supports  
- Coordinate same-week referral to perinatal mental health specialist  
- Supply crisis & 24-h warm-line numbers; instruct to return/re-contact if worsening mood, intrusive thoughts, or emergent self-harm ideas  

Clinician: ___________________  
Credentials: ___________________
